note: Let p=BD/DC, q=CE/EA, r=AF/FB. In normalized barycentric coordinates (x,y,z), D=(0,1/(1+p),p/(1+p)), E=(q/(1+q),0,1/(1+q)), F=(1/(1+r),r/(1+r),0). Hence AD: z=py, BE: x=qz, CF: y=rx. A common point has nonzero coordinates because positivity of p,q,r propagates any zero through all three equations. Multiplication yields pqr=1. Conversely if pqr=1, (x,y,z)=(q p,1,p)/(qp+1+p) is positive and satisfies all three line equations, giving an interior common point.
